interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body:
The prognosis is influenced by several factors, including a preoperative PSA of 18 ng/mL and an ISUP grade group 3 Gleason pattern from the prostatectomy specimen. Positive findings include negative surgical margins and no seminal vesicle invasion or lymphovascular invasion documented. A significant limitation is that no lymph nodes were removed, meaning nodal status cannot be assessed, which widens uncertainty regarding risk stratification. The biopsy-to-prostatectomy comparison is limited as the pathology report notes missing Gleason pattern and ISUP grade from the initial biopsy session.

The trajectory of postoperative PSA remains unknown, and further follow-up data would significantly revise this prognosis. Given the current findings, the prognostic assessment relies heavily on the absence of local recurrence signs at the surgical site. The remaining information needed to refine risk stratification includes nodal status confirmation and serial measurements of the postoperative PSA. The fixed estimated horizon is 62.79 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 40.81–84.77 months; its coverage has not been validated.
